questions.question: Explain how a rise in interest rates from 2% to 5% might affect a business that has a large bank loan.
questions.correctAnswer: Higher interest rates increase loan repayments, reducing profit margins. The business may cut investment, delay expansion, or raise prices. Consumers also have less disposable income (higher mortgage payments), so demand may fall. However, savers earn more interest, which could benefit some customer groups.

questions.question: Analyse how a strengthening of the pound against the euro would affect a UK business that exports to France.
questions.correctAnswer: A stronger pound means UK goods become more expensive for French buyers (they get fewer pounds per euro), making exports less competitive. The business may lose orders to cheaper competitors. However, if the business imports raw materials priced in euros, those inputs become cheaper, partially offsetting the export disadvantage.

questions.question: Evaluate whether a recession is always bad for businesses.
questions.correctAnswer: Some businesses suffer in recession (luxury goods, travel, restaurants) as consumers cut discretionary spending. However, some benefit: discount retailers (Aldi, Lidl) gain customers trading down; repair services grow as people fix rather than replace; essential goods (food, energy) remain in demand.
